data.title: Crypto News | 10-Year Yields Hit 5.04%, Bitcoin Falls to $76K, Clarity Act Odds Halve — The Fed Decides Tomorrow and the BOJ Friday
data.description: The 10-year Treasury yield cleared 5% for the first time since October 2023 and the 30-year hit 5.40% — its highest since June 2007 — as the curve steepened ahead of Wednesday's near-certain 25bps Fed hike. Bitcoin lost the 50-week EMA at $77,430 it reclaimed Monday, falling to $76,000 as 92 of the CoinDesk 100 constituents declined. Clarity Act odds halved on Polymarket to 17-18% after Democrats tabled a counterproposal hours before Tuesday's cloture vote. Strategy passed Ford by market cap with its Bitcoin position up less than 1%. The BOJ decision Friday is the one that matters most for crypto — a carry trade unwind is mechanical selling that correlation data doesn't capture.Bitcoin Slides to $76,000 as the 50-Week EMA Reclaim Fails and Yields Hit 5.04%Bitcoin fell 4.4% from Monday's $79,530 overnight high to $76,000 — losing the 50-week EMA at $77,430 it had just reclaimed and breaking below the $77,100 floor of the Bitfinex spot absorption zone. The 10-year reached 5.04%, the level QCP had described pre-CPI as "the worst mix for Bitcoin: a competing 5% risk-free rate without the nominal-growth impulse that usually accompanies yield moves." A level reclaimed and then lost carries the opposite implication of one that breaks and recovers — Friday's $76,046 dip was bought within the session; Tuesday's slide was not. Put options turned marginally pricier than calls for the first time since the August recovery: 7-day 25-delta skew moved from +2.16v to -1.05v. The BOJ decision Friday at 1.25% is the most consequential remaining event for crypto — carry unwind is mechanical selling that Bitcoin's -0.17 yield correlation does not insulate it from. ﻿US Index Futures Reverse Into the Red With the Dow Down 0.74% Before the FedUS futures turned uniformly lower — Dow -0.74%, Nasdaq -0.71%, S&P 500 -0.60% — reversing morning gains and confirming a macro rather than sectoral driver. Monday's selloff was semiconductor-specific; Tuesday's uniform weakness across Dow, S&P, and Nasdaq describes something broader. Four pressures converged simultaneously: 10-year at 5.04%, Brent above $107, 94% Fed hike odds, and AI uncertainty after Amodei's weekend call — each individually manageable, arriving together without the usual offsets. The long end is doing the damage: in Asian trading the 10-year rose 6.2bps against the 2-year's 4.4bps, steepening the curve and reversing Friday's CPI-driven flattening. ING: "Logically, a rate hike should have calmed the long end, yet the long end is typically extremely volatile." Crypto fell alongside equities Tuesday rather than against them — Bitcoin's Monday decoupling did not repeat.The 30-Year Tops 5.40% and the 10-Year Clears 5% as the Curve Steepens Into the FedThe 30-year hit 5.40% — its highest since June 2007 — while the 10-year cleared 5% for the first time since October 2023. The curve's reversal is the analytical core: Friday's CPI produced flattening (2-year led, 10-year flat), reading as a market treating Fed response as adequate. Tuesday's steepening (10-year +6.2bps, 2-year +4.4bps) says the long end is pricing something the policy rate doesn't fix. Mischler's Tom di Galoma identified four drivers — rate expectations, debt supply, growth prospects, and fiscal trajectory — only the first of which resolves when the tightening cycle ends. Stanley Druckenmiller called Fed members describing policy as restrictive "just ridiculous," adding yields "if anything seem a little low." Bessent's buyback program drew $10.5B in tenders, accepted $5.2B below its own ceiling, and yields sat near session highs afterward — CNBC's Oliver Renick: a public buyer committed at any price removes the incentive to sell early. Tanker rates hit $1M per day for the first time ever, up from under $100,000 a year ago — an inflation input that passes through to every refined product moved by sea.Clarity Act Odds Halve on Polymarket as Democrats Table a Counterproposal Hours Before the VotePolymarket odds on the CLARITY Act being signed into law this year fell from 30-34% to 17-18% after Democrats crafted a counterproposal rejecting the revised 630-page Republican draft circulated Sunday. Tuesday's 2:15pm ET cloture vote requires ~60 votes — approximately 7 Democratic votes beyond the Republican base. The sticking point remains ethics language around officials' crypto holdings, not the market structure framework itself. ARP Digital's Yusuf Fakhro: "Downside from a failed vote is largely priced; a surprise passage is not." Siebert's Brian Vieten offered the dissenting view — a failure pulls product launches and tokenization work into 2027-2028 rather than shelving them. FxPro's Kuptsikevich: total crypto market cap at $2.65T matches May levels, when prediction markets gave CLARITY better than 75% odds — "the market is getting used to life without this legislation." Uniswap held its bid amid the selloff (+1% to $6.60), with more riding on the vote than most DeFi protocols.Strategy Passes Ford by Market Cap With Its Bitcoin Position Up Less Than 1%Strategy's market cap surpassed Ford's, making it the 200th largest US public company — with 845,050 BTC worth ~$64.2B against a $63.7B cost basis at $75,385 average. The position is up approximately 0.8%, roughly $520M on a $63.7B outlay. The company is allocating capital by buying back STRC preferred ($139.3M last week, $635.2M total, authorization doubled to $2B) rather than purchasing Bitcoin — a judgment that the discount on its securities offers better value than the asset at current prices. Strive is running the opposite playbook: 469 BTC acquired last week at par-value SATA preferred issuance, bringing holdings to 25,000 BTC. Same instrument type, opposite direction, determined entirely by where the preferred trades relative to par. STRC at $98.64 gives Strategy reason to buy back; SATA at par lets Strive keep issuing to buy Bitcoin.

data.title: Binance Expands AI-Driven Risk Systems to Protect Users and Reduce Fraud Losses in 2026
data.description:
Binance Blog published a new article, revealing how its AI-driven risk systems are being used to protect users, reduce fraud, and strengthen compliance and internal operations. In the first half of 2026, Binance said these systems helped protect more than 8 million users and prevent approximately $4.6 billion in potential losses. The company said the protections covered abnormal trading activity, account takeover attempts, scams, and transaction fraud. Binance also said AI now informs 80% to 90% of real-time risk decisions across identity verification, account security, payments, and transaction screening, while human reviewers handle edge cases that require more detailed judgment. The article explains how in-house and external models work together, why human oversight remains important, and how the same approach is being applied beyond loss prevention to compliance and internal workflows.

Binance said it intercepted millions of scam and phishing attempts in H1 2026, blacklisted more than 42,000 malicious addresses, and issued over 14,000 real-time warnings daily. The company said these results are supported by more than 100 AI models used across anti-fraud and anti-scam controls. Human risk analysts set thresholds, review unusual cases, and retrain models as new scam patterns appear. In KYC identity verification, Binance said AI-enabled review pipelines have delivered up to 100x operational efficiency gains over manual processes in specific workflows, while specialists remain involved in higher-risk cases. The article also said AI is embedded across the user journey, including identity verification, account security, payments, and broader transaction protection and screening, allowing most checks to be resolved automatically without slowing legitimate users. Binance described its approach as a hybrid model stack that combines proprietary systems with external AI and foundation models, while an internal Red Team tests defenses against realistic attack methods. Chief Security Officer Jimmy Su said these exercises help identify weaknesses before attackers do and strengthen the people, processes, and technology protecting users.

data.title: Bitcoin News | Strategy Passes Ford by Market Cap With Its Bitcoin Position Up Less Than 1%
data.description: Bitcoin treasury company Strategy's market capitalisation has surpassed that of US automaker Ford, making it the 200th largest publicly listed company in the United States, according to BitcoinTreasuries.NET.The company holds 845,050 BTC, unchanged after making no purchases or sales last week.The Underlying Position Is Barely ProfitableThe milestone arrives at an awkward moment for the holdings that justify it.At roughly $76,000 per Bitcoin, Strategy's stack is worth approximately $64.2 billion. Its cost basis of $75,385 puts the acquisition value near $63.7 billion.That leaves the position up roughly 0.8% — around $520 million on a $63.7 billion outlay.A company can be the 200th largest in the US while its core asset sits fractionally above water, because market capitalisation reflects what investors will pay for the structure rather than the mark on the holdings. But the gap is worth stating plainly, because the ranking invites an assumption of accumulated gains that the cost basis does not support.Bitcoin cleared that cost basis in late August during the run from $62,000 to $82,284. It has been oscillating around it since.The Comparison Is to a Company That Makes ThingsFord operates factories, employs a large workforce, generates revenue from vehicle sales and services, and carries the associated capital intensity and cyclical exposure.Strategy holds Bitcoin and issues securities to buy more of it.Comparing the two by market capitalisation is arithmetically valid and analytically odd. One valuation rests on discounted future cash flows from an operating business; the other rests on an asset price plus whatever premium investors assign to the vehicle holding it.That premium is the whole question for Strategy shareholders, and it is not a question Ford's valuation involves at all.Strategy Is Buying Back Preferred Rather Than BitcoinThe capital allocation tells a different story from the milestone.The company repurchased 1.4 million shares of its STRC preferred for $139.3 million using cash on hand, while making no Bitcoin purchases. STRC trades at $98.64, modestly below its $100 par value.Total STRC buybacks have now reached roughly $635.2 million, with the authorisation doubled to $2 billion from $1 billion.A treasury company spending cash to repurchase its own preferred rather than acquiring the asset it exists to hold is making a specific judgment: that the discount on its securities offers better value than the asset at current prices.That is defensible capital allocation. It is also a different activity from what the market capitalisation ranking implies the company is doing.Strive Is Running the Opposite PlaybookThe contrast with the other Bitcoin treasury issuer is now several weeks old.Strive acquired 469 Bitcoin last week, bringing holdings to 25,000 BTC, funded by selling its SATA preferred stock — which continues to trade right around its $100 par value.SATA at par lets Strive keep issuing to buy Bitcoin. STRC below par gives Strategy reason to buy back instead.Same instrument type, opposite direction, determined entirely by where the security trades relative to its stated value. The mechanism connecting preferred pricing to Bitcoin accumulation runs through both companies in reverse.The Ranking Moves With Three VariablesThe 200th-largest position is not a fixed achievement.It shifts with Bitcoin's price, with the premium investors assign to Strategy's structure, and with the valuations of every company ranked near it. Ford's own market capitalisation moves independently.Bitcoin fell to around $76,000 Tuesday, losing the 50-week exponential moving average at $77,430 it reclaimed Monday and breaking below the $77,100 level Bitfinex analysts had identified as the floor of a spot absorption zone.MSTR was flat pre-market Monday.The Fed decides Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. ET, with markets pricing roughly 94% odds of a 25 basis point increase and the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.04%, its highest since July 2007.

data.title: Crypto News | Clarity Act Odds Halve on Polymarket as Democrats Table a Counterproposal Hours Before the Vote
data.description: Polymarket odds on the Clarity Act being signed into law this year fell by roughly half overnight, sliding from around 30% to 34% on Monday to 17% to 18%.The drop followed news that Democrats crafted a counterproposal after rejecting a revised draft Republican negotiators circulated Sunday.Bitcoin gave back Monday's rally, falling 1.7% since midnight UTC to $76,862 after touching $79,427. Ether fell 1.6% to $2,474.76 and Solana lost 2% to $100.43.The Sticking Point Is Ethics, Not Market StructureThe provisions holding up the bill are not the ones the industry cares about.Negotiations have stalled over ethics language governing officials' crypto holdings rather than the market structure framework itself. Several Democrats who might otherwise vote for the bill said they had concerns about the revised ethics proposal.That distinction matters for reading the outcome. A failure would not signal Senate opposition to splitting oversight between the SEC and CFTC. It would signal an unresolved dispute over a provision adjacent to the bill's purpose.Senate Republicans released a revised 630-page draft folding in scores of Democratic provisions in an attempt to reach 60 votes.The Vote Decides Debate, Not PassageTuesday's 2:15 p.m. ET vote is procedural.Clearing cloture opens the bill for floor debate. To become law it must still pass the full Senate, and both chambers must reconcile and pass an identical version before it reaches the President's desk."CLARITY is still far from becoming law even with this, and if it stalls I'd expect the crypto equities to give back more than BTC, given again the beta," said Adam Morgan McCarthy, lead researcher at LO:TECH.McCarthy noted the vote requires approximately seven Democratic votes to reach the 60-vote threshold, with ethics provisions surrounding the president's personal crypto holdings unresolved.The count is the first hard number on how much Senate support the bill actually has.Fakhro: Failure Is Priced, Passage Is NotARP Digital partner Yusuf Fakhro identified the asymmetry."Downside from a failed vote is largely priced; a surprise passage is not," he said.That reading follows from the positioning. Funding rates have drifted toward zero, futures premiums have fallen below 5% and open interest has stalled.Thin leverage means no pile of forced sellers waiting to be liquidated. It also means nothing anchors price, so each headline pushes Bitcoin further than it should.Last week demonstrated the effect. Bitcoin ripped 5% to $81,000 Thursday on softer Fed signals, then gave the entire move back within hours when strong payrolls revived hike expectations.US Buyers Are Sitting on Their HandsCMC head of research Alice Liu pointed to the geographic split in demand."BTC open interest is down about 3.5% over seven days alongside price, and the Coinbase premium has turned slightly negative, which tells you US spot demand is sitting on its hands into the vote," she said.Bitcoin trading at a discount on Coinbase relative to offshore venues is the clearest expression of that. The premium measures US institutional demand against global flow, and a negative reading means US buyers are paying less rather than bidding up.Liu noted spot Bitcoin ETFs saw around $300 million of net outflows over five sessions before a $160 million inflow Monday.The Market Has Already Adjusted to Life Without the BillFxPro chief market analyst Alex Kuptsikevich made the observation that reframes the stakes.Total crypto market capitalisation sits at $2.65 trillion, roughly where it traded in May — when prediction markets gave the Clarity Act better than a 75% chance of passing this year."It appears the market is getting used to life without this legislation," Kuptsikevich said.The market touched $2.71 trillion Tuesday, matching last week's high, before sliding as Democrats tabled their counterproposal.Siebert Argues the Outcome Matters Less Than Traders AssumeBrian Vieten, senior research analyst at Siebert Financial, offered the dissenting view."We think the market is a bit too focused on whether Clarity passes," he said.A failure would leave US firms operating under the current SEC and CFTC approach, which Vieten said could pull product launches and tokenization work forward into 2027 and 2028 rather than shelving them.That cuts against the conventional reading, in which a failure shelves market structure legislation until after November's midterms.Positioning Is Balanced Into the VoteThe long-short taker-volume ratio in crypto futures remains finely balanced.Cumulative open interest fell 1% to $135 billion over 24 hours while trading volume surged 54% to $207 billion — existing participants closing positions faster than new ones open.Bitcoin's pullback to $77,000 was marked by taker selling in futures, according to Marex, with open interest hovering below 680,000 BTC and signalling weak demand for leveraged exposure.Open interest in ether, Solana and XRP futures also remains in a downtrend. Solana's recently stood at 58.81 million tokens, the lowest since May, per CoinGlass.Funding rates are moderately positive for most major tokens including Bitcoin. Ether and Solana carry mildly negative readings implying a slight short bias — positioning that could fuel a squeeze if cloture clears.Put options have turned marginally pricier than calls. Laevitas noted BTC seven-day 25-delta skew moved from +2.16v to −1.05v, and 30-day from +1.33v to −1.39v, across a calendar covering the Senate vote, Wednesday's Fed decision and Friday's BOJ meeting.Selling Was Near Universal92 of the CoinDesk 100 constituents fell on the day, with the index down 1.6%.Traditional markets moved the other way. Nasdaq 100 futures gained 0.43% and S&P 500 futures 0.35% as some of Monday's AI-driven selloff reversed, while the Dollar Index rose 0.17% — making Tuesday a crypto-specific decline and reversing the pattern of 24 hours earlier.Filecoin's 27% Monday surge, which arrived alongside a 70% jump in futures open interest, unwound at speed. It fell 5.1% since midnight to $0.89 and 13% over 24 hours, with open interest down 23% to $106 million.AI and computing tokens took the brunt for a second session following Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's weekend call to slow AI development. Internet Computer was worst at 6% lower to $2.58, with Theta down 4.5% and NEAR 3.7%.Uniswap held its bid while the rest of DeFi sold off, adding 1% to $6.60 and 4.8% over 24 hours — a corner of the market with more riding on the vote than most. XRP rose more than 2% to $1.41 and Zcash nearly 3% to about $1,149.Stellar's XLM was the derivatives outlier, up 4% over 24 hours with futures open interest rising more than 10% to 1 billion XLM and annualised funding at 10% — long accumulation without overheating.CoinMarketCap's Altcoin Season index sits at 36/100, neutral after fading last week's surge to 51/100.

data.title: Carlyle CEO Harvey Schwartz Says the Fed Is Unlikely to Raise Rates Repeatedly
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Carlyle Group CEO Harvey Schwartz said the Federal Reserve is unlikely to raise rates repeatedly even though markets appear to have priced in rate-hike expectations, and he said U.S. economic data remain strong despite conflicts in Europe and Iran and persistent inflation. Schwartz said on Tuesday that the Federal Reserve is expected to keep watching economic data, adding that markets clearly expect rate hikes but it does not feel like the economy is entering a rate-hike cycle or a sharp rate-cut cycle.

data.title: Market News | Four Pressures Converge on Equities With the Fed Decision a Day Away
data.description: European stocks opened broadly lower again, with selling in Italy particularly heavy and the overall backdrop firmly risk-off.Brent crude traded above $107 a barrel after another attack on Saudi energy infrastructure this week sparked fresh supply concerns. The 10-year US Treasury yield rose above 5.02%, its highest since October 2023.US futures pointed lower, with S&P 500 futures down about 0.4% and Nasdaq futures 0.3% after Wall Street was led lower by technology stocks.No Single Variable Explains ItThe distinguishing feature of this session is that nothing in particular went wrong.Oil above $100, Treasury yields above 5%, a more hawkish Fed outlook and lingering AI uncertainty are each individually manageable. Arriving together, they remove the offsets that normally cushion any one of them.An energy shock usually coincides with growth expectations that support earnings. Rising yields usually accompany an expanding economy. AI weakness usually occurs against a supportive rate backdrop.None of those offsets is currently available, and that is what separates a broad decline from a rotation.Italian Banks Are the Specific Weak PointItaly's benchmark index led the decline after a sharp selloff the previous session, with bank stocks especially under pressure again.That concentration is not incidental. Italian banks carry substantial sovereign debt on their balance sheets, which makes them the most direct equity expression of European long-end yield moves.Long-dated sovereign yields have hit multi-decade highs simultaneously across the US, Japan, Germany and France. The ECB raised its deposit rate to 2.5% last week while lifting its 2027 and 2028 inflation outlook, with Deutsche Bank's Mark Wall saying another December move now looks "more likely than not."A bank holding government paper at pre-repricing prices faces mark-to-market pressure that has nothing to do with its lending book.Yesterday's selloff also hit technology names, with Prysmian and STMicroelectronics among those affected.The Long End Is Doing More Damage Than the Policy RateWednesday's decision addresses overnight funding. The move pressuring equities is happening further out the curve.The 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.40%, its highest since June 2007. The 10-year rose 6.2 basis points to 5.021%, outpacing the two-year's 4.4 basis point move to 4.676% — a steepening that reverses the flattening Friday's CPI produced.ING rate strategists noted the disconnect: "Logically, a rate hike should have calmed the long end, yet the long end is typically extremely volatile."Mischler Financial's Tom di Galoma attributed the move to rate expectations, increased corporate and government debt supply, growth prospects and concern about the long-term US fiscal path. "Our budget, deficit, and overall debt structure continue to expand," he said.Only the first of those four resolves when a tightening cycle ends.Technology Carries the Most Duration RiskEquities weighted toward cash flows years forward reprice hardest against a rising long end, which is why technology led both sessions.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 5.9% Monday in its worst session since July 1, with the Nasdaq 100 at a six-week low. Nvidia dropped more than 4% while Intel, Micron and SanDisk each fell over 7%.The AI uncertainty di Galoma's list does not cover has its own source. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for the industry to slow development over the weekend, with OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk agreeing — a warning originating with the people whose revenue depends on the pace continuing.Anthropic separately signed a $13.7 billion six-year compute agreement with Rumble the same day.The Oil Constraint Is PhysicalBrent above $107 reflects a supply bottleneck rather than a risk premium.Saudi Arabia closed the East-West pipeline, which runs to the Red Sea port of Yanbu and exists specifically to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. With Hormuz disrupted and the bypass shut, production fell to 6.238 million barrels per day — the lowest since 1990. Bab El-Mandeb has also come under threat, closing the remaining alternative.A risk premium unwinds when tensions ease. An export bottleneck unwinds only when a route reopens.President Trump suggested Monday that the conflict could end soon, and prices dipped before resuming their climb on the latest infrastructure attack.The Fed Cannot Address Most of ThisMarkets price a 25 basis point increase at roughly 87% to 93% depending on venue, with UBS, HSBC, Barclays, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America and JPMorgan all expecting the move.Their paths diverge sharply after it — UBS at 50 basis points this year, Bank of America at 75, Deutsche Bank running through March 2027, and Jefferies expecting fewer than markets price.QCP Capital identified the bind: continued energy prices could keep the Fed restrictive, while economic data weakness caused by those same costs would argue for patience.Bitcoin traded around $77,000 after crossing $79,000 Monday, having reclaimed its 50-week exponential moving average at $77,430 before slipping back. The decision comes Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. ET, alongside updated projections and a Warsh press conference.

data.title: US Official: Iran Tried to Seize Navy Drone Patrolling the Strait of Hormuz
data.description:
A U.S. official said on Monday that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps used boats in an attempt to capture a U.S. Navy unmanned vessel patrolling the Strait of Hormuz. According to Sina Finance, after the attempted seizure was identified, a U.S. drone fired two missiles at the boats and destroyed them, with most people on board killed.

U.S. Central Command spokesman Colonel Tim Hawkins confirmed the failed seizure attempt, saying Iranian small boats had recently tried to take a U.S. unmanned surface vessel and that Central Command responded forcefully. Hawkins said the unmanned surface vessel remained under U.S. operational control.

The incident came as the United States sought to protect rising commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. A U.S. official said tanker traffic through the strait had begun to be arranged for daytime passage with Gulf countries, rather than only at night as in recent months. Another U.S. official said Saudi Arabia had sharply increased the number of tankers passing through the strait as the conflict in the Red Sea and with the Houthis escalated. The U.S. military has also expanded the mine-clearing security zone along the strait's main shipping lane. On average, 40 ships now cross the strait each day under U.S. guidance and protection, and about 14 million barrels of oil are exported through the waterway daily. Over the past week, several tankers carrying liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas also passed through the strait.

data.title: Musk Teases Possible Tesla-SpaceX Combination
data.description:
Elon Musk again raised the idea of combining SpaceX with Tesla Inc., noting the close cooperation between the two companies he leads as chief executive officer, according to Bloomberg.

Musk made the comment while responding to a question about why Tesla and SpaceX remain separate.
